what_happened: During research reproduction of the V7 untracking scenario, a Bash tool call's leading 'cd $scratchdir' silently failed (scratchpad dir is outside the main working directories, so cd state does not persist across tool calls per the harness contract) and the remaining shell commands in that same call ran against the real repo's cwd instead, writing 'sub/' over the real .gitignore and committing it as 54e80b7fe ('add gitignore for sub'). Caught immediately via git log/git show, fixed by restoring .gitignore from the prior commit and committing the restoration via git-commit-scoped.sh (239f0217e), scoped to .gitignore only. No other files were affected. Immediate git log/git show inspection after the scratch-repo bash call caught the damage before it compounded; git-commit-scoped.sh's single-file pathspec made the corrective commit trivial to scope correctly.

Plan-phase probe invalidated the research report's recommended fix as a COMPLETE fix: four scratch-repo variants show that no pathspec-scoped 'git commit -- <paths>' form (directory pathspec, explicit file list, or --only) can carry a 'git rm --cached' untracking whose content remains on disk -- all exit 1 'nothing to commit' and HEAD does not advance. Only a bare 'git commit' (whole index) lands it. A V2 pre-add carve-out alone therefore stops the silent revert but still cannot commit the untracking; the plan adds a guarded index-equivalence-verified commit path plus a V8 intent-snapshot correction (the V8 pre-commit snapshot would otherwise record the still-on-disk, now-untracked, non-gitignored files as intended-present and flag the correct untracking as exit 5).

Phase 1's scoped suite run (run-all.sh --only ...) surfaced 2 NEW failing suites: test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (25 cases) and test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh (7 cases). Verified by temporarily swapping git-commit-scoped.sh back to the HEAD (pre-edit) copy and re-running both suites: identical failure counts (25 and 7) reproduced against the unmodified script, confirming these are pre-existing defects in reconcile-task-status.sh/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh, not a regression from this phase's git-commit-scoped.sh edit. Neither file is in this task's declared file_scope. Left unfixed; not this task's responsibility.

Phase 5's independent full 'bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh' run (performed before re-consulting the dispatch's own Batch Gate Deferral directive, which supersedes the plan's literal 'no --only-gate narrowing' Phase 5 instruction) reported 4 of 43 checks failing: (1) Gate 8's run-all.sh exited 1 after waiting 210s+ for specs/.gate-lock held by session=verify-deploy-gate8-756977 pid=757095, which was already dead and the lock directory already gone by the time this was investigated -- a transient contention artifact from a concurrently-scheduled sibling task sharing this working tree, not an actual suite failure (no suite output was ever produced). (2) Gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep) exceeded its 60s timeout -- plausibly ambient load from concurrent sibling activity; unrelated to any file this task touched. (3) Whole-tree orphan detection reported 8 findings, all under agent-system/extensions/memory/** (distill-*-submode.md, memory-harvest.sh, memory-retrieve.sh) -- matching the concurrently-scheduled sibling task's own declared territory on the memory extension, not this task's file_scope. (4) Dead-command-recommendation lint reported 2 violations, both in agent-system/extensions/memory/context/project/memory/{memory-setup.md,memory-troubleshooting.md} naming '/ide has no definition file' -- already a documented, tracked pre-existing finding (see this task directory's own Phase 1 issue-log entry quoting the known-failures.txt row covering exactly these two files) and also inside the memory extension's territory, not this task's. None of the 4 failures are attributable to agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh, its test suite, or git-staging-scope.md. Per the dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral directive, this phase's actual verification basis is the scoped 'run-all.sh --only' 16-suite covering set (14 passed, 2 failed -- the same 2 pre-existing out-of-scope failures already recorded in Phases 1-2), not this exploratory full run.
